m: To waste time; to move slowly.
e: 17th-century English, possibly related to daddle (to walk unsteadily).
t: Don't dawdle: « ne traîne pas ».

m: To cause to change direction; to turn aside.
t: Same as « défléchir / déflexion ». Deflect criticism = détourner.

m: To regard as unlikely or unworthy of consideration; to reduce the price of.
f: ne pas tenir compte de; escompter
t: Discount a rumour = ignore it. Beyond price cuts: « ne pas tenir compte ».

m: One who opposes official policy.
t: Same as « dissident »: sits apart.

m: (inform on/against) To betray; (inform) to give shape or character to.
t: inform on someone = « dénoncer ». Also: a decision informed by data.

m: Irritating; tedious.
t: It irks me: « ça m'agace ». An irksome chore.

m: A metal chain for the hands; (v.) to restrain.
t: Latin manus (hand): « menotte ».

m: Unassuming; moderate or limited in size.
t: Same as « modeste »: a modest salary is of limited size.

m: Harmful, poisonous or very unpleasant.
t: Same family as « nocif ». Noxious fumes.

m: A difficult, unpleasant situation.
t: « Prédicament » is not French. Think « pétrin »: in a predicament.

m: Competent or skilled.
t: Pro + facere: progress as a pro. Proficient in French.

m: Using too many words; tediously lengthy.
t: Same as « prolixe »: a verbose essay.

m: Contempt or disdain.
t: Cousin of « escarnir »: to treat with scorn. « Mépriser » = to scorn.

m: Lower in rank or importance.
t: Same as « subordonné ».

m: An assistant or follower.
t: Same as « acolyte » (in English with a mild negative tone).

m: To smear with oil, as a rite; to choose officially.
t: Same as « oindre ». An heir anointed as successor.

m: Persuasion by force or threats.
t: Same as « coercition ».

m: To invent a new word or phrase.
e: Old French coing (wedge, stamp for minting money).
t: Not « coin » (corner)! Coin a term = forger. Money is struck with a coin die.

m: Skilled in deceit; clever in achieving one's ends.
t: Fox-like: « rusé ».

m: To make uneasy or confused.
t: Related to « déconfit »: defeated and embarrassed. Discomfit ≠ discomfort.

m: To purify a liquid; to extract the essential meaning of.
t: Same as « distiller »: drops. Distill a report into key points.

m: Capable of making mistakes.
t: Same as « faillible »: capable of faillir.

m: Nervously awkward and ungainly.
t: Tall, gauche and clumsy: « dégingandé ».

m: Having fine personal qualities or high social rank.
t: Same as « noble ».

m: Of first importance; main.
t: Prime minister: « Premier ministre ».

m: Fundamental; far-reaching; extreme.
t: Same as « radical »: from the root. Radical reform.

m: Relating to time; worldly, not spiritual.
t: Same as « temporel »: temporal power opposes spiritual power.

m: Up to date with; side by side.
t: Keep abreast of the news = rester au courant.

m: A temporary departure from the main subject.
t: Same as « digression ».

m: Deceitful; double-dealing.
t: Duplex = two-faced. Duplicité in French has the same sense.

m: To invent (something false); to make or manufacture.
t: Fabriquer. A fabricated story is invented from scratch.

m: Looking or feeling dejected.
t: Gloomy: « avoir le moral dans les chaussettes ».

m: A person or thing that announces the approach of something.
e: Old French herberger (to lodge), an advance officer arranging lodging.
t: Originally the scout who finds you a bed (auberge). Swallows are a harbinger of spring.

m: Generosity in bestowing gifts or money.
t: Same as « largesse ».

m: A person who behaves without moral restraint.
t: Same as « libertin »: Dom Juan.

m: Clear and obvious; (v.) to display.
t: Same as « manifeste ». Manifest destiny.

m: Extremely small; very precise (pronounced my-NYOOT).
t: Not the time unit: mi-NUTE = tiny, « minutieux ». Minute details.

m: Skill or expertise; bravery in battle.
t: Same as « prouesse ».

m: A split between strongly opposed groups.
t: Same as « schisme »: schizo = split.

m: The making of a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.
t: « Esclandre »: scandal → slander.

m: Applicable to all cases; relating to everyone.
t: Same as « universel ».

m: Very sad; deplorably bad.
t: Full of woe (malheur). Woeful performance = pitoyable.

m: Extremely bad; showing hopelessness or humiliation.
t: Same as « abject ». Abject poverty.

m: Characterized by friendliness; without ill feeling.
t: « Amical ». An amicable divorce = divorce à l'amiable.

m: A concentrated outpouring (of questions, criticism); heavy artillery fire.
t: Un barrage: like a dam bursting. A barrage of questions.

m: To succeed in understanding or reading something unclear.
t: Same as « déchiffrer ».

m: A false belief held despite contrary evidence.
t: « Délire ». Delusions of grandeur = folie des grandeurs.

m: To distribute; (dispense with) to do without.
t: Dispense with formalities = se passer des formalités. Dispenser = distributeur.

m: Courage in pain or adversity.
t: Same family as « fort ».

m: Deserving reward or praise.
t: Same as « méritoire ».

m: An open rebellion against authority, especially by sailors.
t: Same as « mutinerie ».

m: Persistence in doing something despite difficulty.
t: Same as « persévérance ».

m: To cause to be or become; to provide or give.
t: Same as « rendre »: render someone speechless.

m: The stock of skills or pieces a person is prepared to perform.
t: Same as « répertoire ».

m: Able to recover quickly; flexible.
t: Same as « résilient »: bounces back.

m: Admirably purposeful and determined.
t: Same as « résolu ».

m: Bending and moving easily and gracefully.
t: « Souple » → supple.

m: Great courage in the face of danger.
t: Same as « valeur » (in the old sense). « Valeureux ».

m: Striking; capturing the attention.
t: It stops you in your tracks: an arresting photograph.

m: Careful management of resources; thrift.
t: Beyond GDP: economy of words = brièveté, économie de moyens.

m: Relating to the basic, simplest parts.
t: Same as « élémentaire »: « Élémentaire, mon cher Watson ».

m: Characterized by intense excitement and happiness.
t: Same as « euphorique ».

m: To start to lose strength; to speak hesitatingly.
t: Falter = vaciller. His voice faltered.

m: Having or displaying passionate intensity.
t: Same as « fervent ».

m: Not conforming to accepted standards or beliefs.
t: Same as « hétérodoxe »; opposite: orthodox.

m: A person or thing that causes problems; legal responsibility; a debt.
t: Opposite of an asset. Un handicap / « passif ». Product liability = responsabilité du fait des produits.

m: Restricting an allowance; frugal.
t: Not stinging! Stinting = skimping. Opposite of lavish: « sans lésiner » = unstinting.

m: To moderate or mitigate; (n.) disposition or anger.
t: Same as « tempérer ». Temper enthusiasm with caution. Also a bad temper.

m: Not certain or fixed; hesitant.
t: Not « tentative » (an attempt, a try). Tentative plans = provisoire, sous réserve.
